sermon.title: Prophecies to Nine Nations
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Isaiah’s prophecies against nine cities and nations (Isaiah 13–23) and shows how Babylon, Moab, Egypt and Tyre were fulfilled, then looks at the hidden “day of the Lord” passages in them. He says God will show mercy and bring in the heathen as well as His people who have given up their inheritance, and ends with Isaiah 26 on desiring Jesus and God’s judgments teaching righteousness.

chunks.section_question: What are the nine prophecies in Isaiah 13–23, and did Babylon become uninhabited as foretold? (Isaiah 13:17-20)
chunks.short_answer: He lists the nine cities or nations Isaiah addresses (Babylon, Moab, Damascus, Egypt, “the desert of the sea,” the valley of vision, Tyre and Sidon, and others) and says Babylon was “a tremendous city” that God said would never be inhabited again. He shows a picture of its ruins today and says “this Bible is a very powerful book” whose prophecies were fulfilled just as spoken, which only a supernatural God can do.

First he talks about, in Isaiah 13, chapters 13 23, he talks about Babylon. Okay, then he talks about Moab. Moab is the incestuous offspring of Lot and his two daughters that got him drunk, all right, and had sex with their father. Then he is going to talk about Damascus, the capital of Syria, the N the nation or empire of Syria. And then he’s going to talk about Egypt, number four. And then he’s going to call something “the desert of the sea,” and this threw me for a for a loop for quite a few years, “the desert of the sea.” And commentaries and all that said that’s the wind blowing in from this sea and destruction of Babylon. Okay, he’s going to talk about the these nine cities or nations.

Now, our opponents are always saying that, you know, God said he would do things and then in the New Testament people just made it happen because they already wrote it, so they just acted on it and said it was fulfilled. But how do you say a tremendous city like Babylon, it was a tremendous city if you know your history, and God says will never be inhabited again. And folks, here’s a picture of it today. Looks pretty in uninhabited, doesn’t it? And there’s many things you see. You can say that God’s going to come in the flesh, give his life, die and resurrect himself again. You see, and the Roman Empire tried their best to distort and destroy that story, but they couldn’t find the evidence. There was nobody. He did rise from the grave, and so forth.

All right, and Assyria was broken, and Palestine right here down in Canaan was also broken. None of these nations ever amounted to anything after God spoke and said they weren’t.

Assyria is the nation God used to correct his people, but they overcorrected, and God raised up Babylon to correct them. Are you there? “A blessing in the midst of the land. So I try to get through the wall. It’s an invisible wall, but the wall is called salvation, all right? And I go up there and I going to go through this wall, and bam, it knocks me back.

Okay, and it lights up and says, “Have you believed on the Lord Jesus Christ and his blood to forgive you and save you from sin?” “No, but I want in.” Bam, another light lights up and says, “Have you kept his commandments to enter into this eternal city?” “No, but I want in.” Bam. I can’t get in, because salvation is its wall. I can only get in through salvation. I can’t get in any other way, and there’s no salvation in any other name but the name of Jesus. Say the name, Jesus. Don’t be ashamed of that name. It’s powerful. And when you’re praising God, if you can’t say anything else, just say Jesus. Man, it’s powerful thing to praise. So I try one more time. Bam, another light lights up and says, “Go to the gate.” “Well, I want to go... go to the gate?” “Go to the gate, you’re not getting in.” So I go to the gate. “Open the gates, so the people keeping the what truth may enter in.” Oh man, I knew that. That’s why I didn’t want to go to the gate. I don’t want to keep the truth, I don’t want... I want to do my thing and I want to go to heaven, I want eternal life. I go to the gate and guess who’s there? Jesus, the truth. What’s he got in his hand? The Bible, the scriptures. The scriptures are truth. And he’s going to say, “Are you keeping the truth?” And I have to, what, admit and say no, I’ve done this, that and the other. And once I confess, what happens? He forgives me. I’m cleansed. And if I got so much pride I won’t confess, I’m turned away, I don’t get in. Are you there, church? Hallelujah.

chunks.section_question: What does desire for Jesus have to do with worship, and why do God’s judgments teach righteousness? (Isaiah 26:8-19)
chunks.short_answer: He says a big key is letting the Holy Ghost put in us a desire for Jesus, not for what we can get from Him. He says “it’s not faith that causes people to live right, it’s not grace… it’s the judgment,” quotes “let grace be shown to the wicked” and “yet he will not learn righteousness,” and says “this flattering gospel of just grace and faith has destroyed the church in America.” He closes with “your dead shall live” and a restoration of the church and the nations.
chunks.text:
Now here is a very important part. they they That’s what worship was about this morning. “I desire you in the night, by my spirit I seek you early.” Morning and night, I desire you, I desire you. I’m not looking for a better job, I’m not looking for a ministry in the church, Jesus, I desire you. Powerful. Most people have never experienced what the woman with the alabaster box experience. She came to Jesus because she loved him. She didn’t even ask for her sins to be forgiven, she didn’t ask anything from him, she just came and loved him, and Jesus forgave her. She desired Jesus. Folks, a big key is we got to let the Holy Ghost put in us a desire for Jesus. People that desire Jesus, they have a drive to come to church, they have a drive to read the Bible, they have a drive to pray. Why? They have a desire that compels them and motivates them, and who is that desire about? Jesus. Not what I can get from him, not my prayer petition, but just him. And that’s going to be a big thing in that day. Hallelujah. And you get your what you need automatically when you touch him. That’s the key.

“When your judgments are in the earth.” Now, what’s the judgment? The arrest, the evidence, the trial, say the sentence, and then the punishment of the reward. “When your judgments are in the earth,” now, young people, this is very important for you to know, young Christians, “the inhabitants of the world will never learn righteousness.” I’m sorry, The inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness I’ve jumped ahead of myself. See, it’s not faith that causes people to live right, it’s not grace that causes people to live right, it’s the judgment. It’s that fear of God that he can bring something in my life to correct me, and eternally correct me if I reject. And so we need, and this is where the American Christian has really blown it since I came into the kingdom, is we haven’t maintained an authoritative position in our government for Bible morality. And now we got kids that don’t have any morals, we got families that don’t have any morals. The humanist and these people that that trample on Bible morality has given us a nation that’s immoral.

Now listen at this, read this with me, ready? “Let grace be shown to the wicked.” Did you read that? Let’s do it again, let’s do it with authority: “Let grace be shown to the wicked.” Yeah, hallelujah. All you hear today is grace and faith, okay. “Let grace, favor, be shown to the wicked,” and what does the prophet say? “Yet he will not learn righteousness.” Why? Because because it’s the judgments that teach righteousness. And folks, that’s the way it is in the kingdom. God wants to correct us, and this this flattering gospel of just grace and faith has destroyed the church in America and weakened it tremendously. Are you out there?

“You’re dead shall live and they shall arise.” And it says a lot of good stuff. I just took some excerpts out of this, it’s very powerful. “Your dead shall live and they shall arise.” See, these people in the world, they going to live and they will arise. As Christians, are going to live and we’re going to arise. The whole purpose of God is for us to, what, live and arise out of trespasses and sin and live a life for Christ. Can I hear an amen? Now, is there a big thing coming up here according to Isaiah? Yes. And you younger ones have a chance to be in part of this. I’ve been in part of this, but it’s obvious I’m going to miss out on some of this good stuff here. But you young people have a tremendous thing to look forward to: the the restoration of the church in America, the restoration of the nation in America, the restoration of the nations of the world, God showing himself that he’s God in a powerful way. You may get to see, and you will see, a lot more of that, and I’ve seen, and I’ve showed you that we’ve be we’ve been able to see it since Azusa, in fact since Luther put his thesis on the wall. It’s been a process, but we’re in the end of this process, and tremendous things are going to happen. Amen.

Let grace be shown to the wicked, Yet he will not learn righteousness; In the land of uprightness he will deal unjustly, And will not behold the majesty of the LORD.

And behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at the table in the Pharisee’s house, brought an alabaster flask of fragrant oil, and stood at His feet behind Him weeping; and she began to wash His feet with her tears, and wiped them with the hair of her head; and she kissed His feet and anointed them with the fragrant oil.

faqs.question: What does he say a “burden” is in the prophets?
faqs.answer: He says “the burden means utterance, divine utterances, prophetic utterances” to natural cities and kingdoms. He says God sometimes hides a second message in them: “that’s how he makes them a mystery.”

faqs.question: Why does he say prophecy switches from nations to the day of the Lord?
faqs.answer: He says God will be “speaking directly to like Egypt” and then “all of a sudden he switches.” He says “that’s how he hides things in his scriptures, that’s how he makes them a mystery.”

faqs.question: What does he say “the day of the Lord” means?
faqs.answer: He says it is the time when the Lord comes, “the period before he comes,” and “a period of what he’s doing at the time he’s doing it.” He says each generation can experience what God is doing in its day of the Lord.

faqs.question: Does he say man will destroy the world with weapons?
faqs.answer: He says that back in the 1950s everyone preached God would use the atomic bomb to destroy the world, and answers “God don’t need man’s help when he is going to do something.” He says this destruction “comes from God and people are going to know it’s from God.”

faqs.question: What does he mean by an “Israelite Christian”?
faqs.answer: He says Israel was the northern kingdom that “worship God with things they devised in their own heart,” never had a good king, and served God “the way they thought was appropriate for their mind.” He says a tip-off is the statement “well, I believe,” as if believing justifies everything.

faqs.question: Does he say believers must escape the great day of the Lord?
faqs.answer: He says people who don’t know the Bible “think we got to escape this great time of the Lord,” but “he is going to be merciful to us during it, that means we’re not going to be destroyed.” He says “it’s going to pay to serve Jesus in that day.”

faqs.question: Why does he say we must admit we are wrong?
faqs.answer: He says “you can believe for righteousness, but until you admit you’re wrong and you repent and turn, you’re not saved.” He cites that with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

scriptures.text_nkjv: that if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, you will be saved. For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

faqs.question: What does he say about the pre-tribulation rapture teaching?
faqs.answer: He says people tell others they will not make it if they are not saved before the rapture, and that he has dealt with people who tried to commit suicide because of it. He says “that pre-tribulation rapture thing is very destructive.”

faqs.question: Why does he say you do not have to bend the scriptures?
faqs.answer: He says “the scriptures are uniform throughout,” so “you don’t have to rubber band scriptures and bend them and stretch them.” He says there are seven things that will happen in that day.

faqs.question: Why does he say the wise men’s star could not be a normal star?
faqs.answer: He says the nearest star is the sun and if it were moved closer we would boil, so they could not follow it to a specific house, and it disappeared and reappeared. He says it could have been an angel or “a little sun” God made, and that “it’s a supernatural event.”

faqs.question: What does he say about the word of knowledge?
faqs.answer: He says it was added in the late 1940s: people “actually could foretell people’s lives, tell them about themselves accurately,” and God would heal or transform them. He says it brought a powerful presence and worship, with churches praising God for an hour.

faqs.question: What does he say about the 1960s outpouring in the denominations?
faqs.answer: He says God poured out His Spirit on Episcopalians, Anglicans, Presbyterians, Lutherans, Methodists and Baptists, and in 1967 on the Catholic Church, and “he didn’t ask the Pope’s permission or anybody’s permission.” He says the Jesus people came along in the 1970s.

faqs.question: Does he say God loves people of every nation?
faqs.answer: He says “God loves everybody in the earth. He created them and wants to bring them in,” and lists Eskimos, Mongolians and the people of the islands of the sea. He also says God loves Muslims.

faqs.question: What does he say about ministers in that day?
faqs.answer: He says “ministers are going to be nothing” and “we need to learn to be like John the Baptist: we must decrease and he must increase.” He says too many ministers are letting people worship them and put their trust in them.

scriptures.text_nkjv: He must increase, but I must decrease.

faqs.question: How does he sum up the gospel?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus was born of a virgin, did signs and wonders, preached the kingdom of God, laid down His life, rose from the grave and ascended for the sins of the world, and “if you call on him he will forgive you, cleanse you and empower you to become a son of God.”
